an8.51:1.1: At one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Sakiyans, near to Kapilavatthu, in Nigrodha’s Monastery.
an8.51:1.2: Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Fortunate One, ‘Approached the Fortunate One’ means the Fortunate One, having gone to Kapila’s city, Having gone into the presence of Mahāpajāpatī, The five hundred (wives) approached Mahāpajāpatī, Having taken those women, Mahāpajāpatī approached the Fortunate One. and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, she stood on one side. While standing on one side Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:1.3: “It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:1.5: Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, ‘Enough,
an8.51:2.1: Gotamī! Please do not wish,’ is said. Why did he refuse? the going forth from the home to the homeless life.” For a second time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:2.2: “It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:2.4: Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:3.1: For a third time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:3.2: “It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:3.4: Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.” Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, thinking: ‘The Fortunate One does not allow for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life,’
an8.51:4.1: pained and depressed, crying, with tears on her face, having worshipped and circumambulated the Fortunate One,
an8.51:5.1: went away. Then the Fortunate One, having dwelt in Kapilavatthu for as long as he liked, ‘Dwelt for as long as he liked’ means went on walking tour towards Vesālī,
an8.51:5.2: and while walking gradually on walking tour he arrived at Vesālī.
an8.51:5.3: There the Fortunate One dwelt near Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Gabled Hall.
an8.51:5.4: Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, after having her hair cut off, and donning ochre clothes, together with a great many Sakiyan ladies, went towards Vesālī, ‘Together with a great many Sakiyan ladies’ means together with a great many Sakiyan ladies, (she went towards Vesālī).
an8.51:5.5: and gradually approached the Great Wood, and the Gabled Hall at Vesālī.
an8.51:5.6: Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, with swollen feet, and dust on her limbs, ‘With swollen feet’ means Therefore it was said: ‘With swollen feet.’ pained and depressed, crying, with tears on her face, stood outside the doorway.
an8.51:6.1: Venerable Ānanda saw Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, with swollen feet, and dust on her limbs, pained and depressed, crying, with tears on her face, stood outside the doorway. ‘Outside the doorway’ means outside the doorway.
an8.51:6.2: And after seeing (her), he said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
an8.51:6.3: “Why are you, Gotamī, with swollen feet, and dust on your limbs, ‘Why are you, Gotamī?’ means (he was asking): with swollen feet, standing (there)? pained and depressed, crying, with tears on your face, standing outside the doorway?”
an8.51:6.4: “Because, venerable Ānanda, the Fortunate One does not allow for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:6.5: “Then, Gotamī, just wait here, while I request the Fortunate One for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:7.1: Then venerable Ānanda approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:7.2: “This Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, reverend Sir, with swollen feet, and dust on her limbs, pained and depressed, crying, with tears on her face, is standing outside the doorway,
an8.51:7.3: thinking: ‘The Fortunate One does not allow for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.’
an8.51:7.4: It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:7.6: Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:8.1: For a second time...pe... venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One: “It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.” “Enough, Ānanda! Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:8.2: For a third time venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:8.3: “It is good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:8.5: Please do not wish for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:9.1: Then it occurred to venerable Ānanda:
an8.51:9.2: ‘The Fortunate One does not allow for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.
an8.51:9.3: What if I were to ask the Fortunate One in a different way ‘In a different way’ means with a different reason. for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life?’
an8.51:9.4: Then venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:9.5: “Is it possible, reverend Sir, for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, having gone forth from the home to the homeless life, ° to directly experience the fruit of Stream Entry, or the fruit of Once-Returning, or the fruit of Non-Returning, or the fruit of Liberation?”
an8.51:9.6: “It is possible, Ānanda, that women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, having gone forth from the home to the homeless life, ° to directly experience the fruit of Stream Entry, and the fruit of Once-Returning, and the fruit of Non-Returning, and the fruit of Liberation.”
an8.51:9.7: “If it is possible, reverend Sir, for women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, having gone forth from the home to the homeless life, ° to directly experience the fruit of Stream Entry...pe..., and the fruit of Once-Returning, and the fruit of Non-Returning, and the fruit of Liberation,
an8.51:9.8: and Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī was a great help, reverend Sir, ‘A great help, reverend Sir,’ and so forth, she is the Fortunate One’s maternal aunt, his wet-nurse, who looked after him and gave him milk,
an8.51:9.9: and after the Fortunate One’s Mother had died, she gave him suck at the breast.
an8.51:9.10: It would be good, reverend Sir, if women could receive, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, the going forth from the home to the homeless life.”
an8.51:10.1: “If, Ānanda, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts these eight serious rules, this will be the higher ordination for her: ‘If, Ānanda, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts these eight serious rules, this will be the higher ordination for her,’ and so forth was said.
an8.51:11.1: A nun having a hundred years (seniority), in regard to a monk ordained that day, ‘In regard to a monk ordained that day’ means to one ordained on that day. should worship, rise from the seat, salute and pay homage. ‘Should worship, rise from the seat, salute and pay homage’ means (in this way) she should pay homage.
an8.51:11.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:12.1: A nun should not enter the Rains Retreat in a dwelling place without monks. ‘A dwelling place without monks’ means In such a dwelling place they should not undertake the Rains Retreat.
an8.51:12.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:13.1: Every fortnight the nuns are to expect two things from the Community of monks: ‘Every fortnight’ means every Observance day.
an8.51:13.2: asking about the Observance day, and approaching (the monks) for (getting) advice.
an8.51:13.3: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:14.1: A nun emerging from the Rains Retreat should invite both Communities in regard to three reasons:
an8.51:14.2: with what was seen, or what was heard or what was suspected.
an8.51:14.3: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:15.1: A nun who is guilty of a serious offence should observe reparation for a fortnight before both Communities.
an8.51:15.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:16.1: (Only) a trainee who has trained in the six training rules for two years should seek for higher ordination before both Communities.
an8.51:16.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:17.1: A nun should not abuse or censure a monk by any means. ‘Should not abuse or censure’ means
an8.51:17.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:18.1: From today forward nuns are prohibited from speaking (advice) to monks, ‘Nuns are prohibited from speaking (advice) to monks’ means the nuns are barred and prevented from speaking to monks, (but) monks are not prohibited from speaking (advice) to nuns. ‘Monks are not prohibited from speaking (advice) to nuns’ means monks are not barred from speaking to nuns
an8.51:18.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:19.1: If, Ānanda, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts these eight serious rules, that will be her higher ordination.”
an8.51:20.1: Then venerable Ānanda, having learned these eight serious rules in the presence of the Fortunate One, approached Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, and after approaching he said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
an8.51:21.1: “If you, Gotamī, could accept these eight serious rules, this will be for you your higher ordination:
an8.51:22.1: A nun having a hundred years (seniority), in regard to a monk ordained that day, should worship, rise from the seat, salute and pay homage.
an8.51:22.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. A nun should not enter the Rains Retreat in a dwelling place without monks. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. Every fortnight the nuns are to expect two things from the Community of monks: asking about the Observance day, and approaching for (giving) advice. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. A nun emerging from the Rains Retreat should invite both Communities in regard to three reasons: with what was seen, or what was heard or what was suspected. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. A nun who is guilty of a serious offence should observe reparation for a fortnight before both Communities. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. (Only) a trainee who has trained in the six training rules for two years should seek for higher ordination before both Communities. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts. A nun should not abuse or censure a monk by any means. This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:23.1: From today forward nuns are prohibited from speaking (advice) to monks, (but) monks are not prohibited from speaking (advice) to nuns.
an8.51:23.2: This is a rule that should be respected, treated seriously, be honoured, worshipped, and should not be transgressed for as long as her life lasts.
an8.51:23.3: If you, Gotamī, could accept these eight serious rules, that will be for you your higher ordination.” Having learned these eight serious rules in the Teacher’s presence,
an8.51:24.1: “It is as though, venerable Ānanda, a woman or a man, young, youthful, having ornaments, with head washed, had been given a garland of waterlilies, or a garland of jasmine, or a garland of whirlybird flowers, and having accepted it with both hands, were to place it on top of the most important limb, on the head,
an8.51:24.2: just so, venerable Ānanda, I accept these eight serious rules which should not be transgressed for as long as life lasts.”
an8.51:25.1: Then venerable Ānanda approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.51:25.2: “Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, reverend Sir, has accepted the eight serious rules which should not be transgressed for as long as life lasts.”
an8.51:26.1: “If, Ānanda, women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, had not obtained the going forth from the home to the homeless life, Ānanda, the spiritual life would have been long-lasting, the Good Dhamma would have endured for a thousand years.
an8.51:26.2: But because, Ānanda, women, in this Dhamma and Discipline taught by the Realised One, have gone forth from the home to the homeless life, now, Ānanda, the spiritual life will not be long-lasting,
an8.51:26.3: the Good Dhamma, Ānanda, will now endure for (only) five hundred years.
an8.51:27.1: Just as, Ānanda, those families having lots of women and few men, are easily plundered by thieves and night-time robbers,
an8.51:27.2: just so, Ānanda, wherever in this Dhamma and Disciple women receive the going forth from the home to the homeless life, the spiritual life will not be long-lasting.
an8.51:28.1: Just as, Ānanda, in ripe rice fields which go down with the disease called Deadheart, ‘The disease called Deadheart’ means that rice field is not long-lasting,
an8.51:28.2: just so, Ānanda, wherever in this Dhamma and Disciple women receive the going forth from the home to the homeless life, the spiritual life will not be long-lasting.
an8.51:29.1: Just as, Ānanda, in ripe sugar-cane fields which go down with the disease called Red Rot, ‘The disease called Red Rot’ means being reddened on the inside of the sugar cane. that sugar-cane field is not long-lasting,
an8.51:29.2: just so, Ānanda, wherever in this Dhamma and Disciple women receive the going forth from the home to the homeless life, the spiritual life will not be long-lasting.
an8.51:30.1: Just as, Ānanda, a man might prepare an embankment as a precaution round a large lake so that the water does not overflow,
an8.51:30.2: just so, Ānanda, the eight serious rules were laid down by me as a precaution which should not be transgressed for as long as life lasts.” ‘An embankment as a precaution round a large lake,’ the precaution is (taken that) the serious rules that are not to be transgressed are laid down, the Good Dhamma can endure (only) for five hundred years. Thus at first it was said it will endure for one thousand years. ‘One thousand years,’ thus the Good Dhamma of penetration (to Awakening) will endure for five thousand years (in all).
